metadata.subtitle: The DPA-Review Skill
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when Claude reviews a vendor's Data Processing Agreement, is it approving the agreement, or checking it against a fixed list of required clauses? Lands the carry-out that Claude checks the SKILL.md's clause list, one step at a time, and only does what that file says.

beats.narration_text: Someone asked whether Claude approves a vendor's DPA when it reviews one. It doesn't approve — it checks clauses against a fixed list. So: when Claude reviews a DPA, is it checking a list?

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called dpa-review. Its one file, SKILL.md, holds the whole instruction set, written in plain language — no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.
The instructions live in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order and executes it — read the file, execute each step, return the result. Linear: no branching, unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: READ, EXECUTE, RETURN
production_viz.caption: linear — no branching unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: One instruction inside it is specific: check whether the agreement names every sub-processor, and states what happens to the data when the contract ends — deleted, or returned. Those two clauses go missing most often. What the skill doesn't do is judge whether the described security measures are actually strong enough for the data involved — that call needs a person who knows the systems.

production_viz.label: WHAT THE CHECKLIST COVERS
production_viz.caption: checks the list, not whether it's good enough

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't judging whether the agreement is good enough — it's checking the SKILL.md's list of required clauses, one step at a time, and only doing what that file says.

props.sparkLine: Checks the list. Only the list.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: I'm about to sign a vendor's data processing agreement. Read the dpa-review skill, and before you check anything, walk me through exactly what you'll do — which clauses you'll check for, what counts as missing, and what you won't be able to tell me.
